title: The Days of Purim
backstory: Haman is gone, but the law he wrote still stands, for no decree sealed with the king's ring could be recalled. So a new decree must go out, giving God's people the right to stand for their lives. Sorrow is about to turn to joy, and a yearly feast is born so that no generation will ever forget.

passages.synopsis: The king gave Haman's house to Esther, and Mordecai received the king's ring. But the terrible decree still stood, so Esther fell at the king's feet with tears, pleading for her people. The king could not reverse a sealed law, but he told Esther and Mordecai to write a new decree in his name. Whatever they wrote and sealed with the king's ring, no man could undo.

Mordecai went out from the king dressed in royal blue and white, with a great crown of gold. The city of Shushan rejoiced. The Jews had light, and gladness, and joy, and honour. In every province the new decree brought feasting and a good day, and many people of the land joined themselves to God's people.

The Jews were delivered from those who had sought their harm, and their sorrow was turned into joy. Mordecai wrote letters to every province, setting apart two days each year for feasting, for sending portions of food to one another, and for giving gifts to the poor. The days were named Purim, after Pur, the lot that Haman had cast. Every family in every generation was to remember them. Esther the queen and Mordecai wrote once more with all authority, and the decree of Esther confirmed these matters of Purim, and it was written in the book.

The book closes quietly: King Ahasuerus laid a tribute upon the land and upon the isles of the sea. All his power and might, and the greatness of Mordecai, were written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia. Mordecai the Jew was next unto the king, great among the Jews, and accepted of the multitude of his brethren. He sought the good of his people and spoke peace to all his kindred.

triviaQuestions.question: What did Mordecai wear when he went out from the king's presence?
options: Royal apparel of blue and white, with a great crown of gold
triviaQuestions.explanation: Esther 8:15 — "And Mordecai went out from the presence of the king in royal apparel of blue and white, and with a great crown of gold, and with a garment of fine linen and purple: and the city of Shushan rejoiced and was glad."

triviaQuestions.question: Why were the days of celebration called Purim?
options: After the name of Pur, the lot
triviaQuestions.explanation: Esther 9:26 — "Wherefore they called these days Purim after the name of Pur. Therefore for all the words of this letter, and of that which they had seen concerning this matter, and which had come unto them,"

triviaQuestions.question: In which month do the days of Purim fall?
triviaQuestions.explanation: Esther 9:21 — "To stablish this among them, that they should keep the fourteenth day of the month Adar, and the fifteenth day of the same, yearly,"

triviaQuestions.question: Who was next unto King Ahasuerus at the close of the book?
triviaQuestions.explanation: Esther 10:3 — "For Mordecai the Jew was next unto king Ahasuerus, and great among the Jews, and accepted of the multitude of his brethren, seeking the wealth of his people, and speaking peace to all his seed."

scrambleVerses.text: The Jews had light, and gladness, and joy, and honour.
Then the king held out the golden sceptre toward Esther.
And the decree of Esther confirmed these matters of Purim;

reflection: The month was turned from sorrow to joy, and God's people remembered it every year. God's name is never written in this book, yet he watched over his people from the first page to the last. How do you remember and celebrate what God has done for you?
